title: The Spouter-Inn: A Bed Fellow Found
adaptation_principle: Track Ishmael’s lodging problem from offer to acceptance, compressing décor and tavern revelry into set dressing while staging only the decisions and encounters that change his night: conditional agreement, refusal and bench fiasco, retreat to the room, the harpooneer’s return and rite, the midnight scare, and Ishmael’s final acceptance.

Ishmael (narrator).visual_description: Young adult sailor of average build, travel-worn; dark monkey jacket or coarse wool coat and knit cap in the public room; later in shirt-sleeves in the cold upstairs chamber; plain, unadorned look.

Peter Coffin (landlord).visual_description: Lean, middle-aged New England innkeeper with a weathered face; shirtsleeves, vest, and apron; old silk handkerchief at his neck; practical, quick with tools; carries and lights a tallow candle.

Queequeg (harpooneer).role: South Seas harpooneer and future shipmate
Queequeg (harpooneer).visual_description: Tall, powerfully built; purplish-yellow complexion; face, chest, back, arms, and legs tattooed with large dark square patterns; little scalp-knot on the forehead; wears a heavy sea-coat (grego) when entering, later bare-chested; calm, self-possessed; carries a tomahawk-pipe and a large seaman’s bag; handles an embalmed New Zealand head and a small ebony idol.

tomahawk_pipe.visual_description: A combined smoking pipe and small hatchet with a short wooden handle and metal head; ember glows in the bowl when lit.
tomahawk_pipe.avoid_confusion: It is not a separate battle axe; it is the harpooneer’s pipe shaped like a tomahawk.

preserved_New_Zealand_head.visual_description: A small, shriveled, dark, embalmed human head used as a South Seas curiosity; carried carefully by Queequeg.
preserved_New_Zealand_head.avoid_confusion: Show as a preserved artifact without gore or fresh wounds; not a severed head in action.

idol_Yojo.visual_description: A small, polished-ebony, hunch-backed wooden image set upright between the andirons.
idol_Yojo.avoid_confusion: Do not depict as a living creature or baby; it is a rigid wooden idol.

big_inn_bed.visual_description: A prodigious, plain wooden bedstead with homespun sheets and blankets in a small, cold, sparsely furnished room.
big_inn_bed.avoid_confusion: Not a fancy four-poster; keep it rough and oversized for two.

seaman_bag.visual_description: A large, scuffed canvas or sealskin sea-bag with knotted cords at the mouth.
seaman_bag.avoid_confusion: Not a rigid trunk; it is a soft, overstuffed sailor’s bag.

carpenter_plane.visual_description: A hand wood-plane the landlord uses to smooth the bench; curls of fresh shavings peel off.
carpenter_plane.avoid_confusion: Not a power tool; simple wooden-bodied or metal-bodied hand plane.

bar_room_bench.visual_description: A rough wooden settle/bench with carved notches and knots; long and hard.
bar_room_bench.avoid_confusion: Not an upholstered sofa; it’s a bare plank settle.

room_fireplace_with_papered_fireboard.visual_description: An empty fireplace whose opening is covered by a removable papered fireboard with a printed figure striking a whale; sooty bricks and iron andirons behind it.
room_fireplace_with_papered_fireboard.avoid_confusion: No readable text on the paper; do not animate the printed scene.

room_harpoon.visual_description: A tall iron harpoon standing by the head of the bed.
room_harpoon.avoid_confusion: Not a decorative spear; it is a whaleman’s harpoon.

action_oriented_synopsis: I ask the landlord for a bed and, with the house full, agree to share with a harpooneer if he proves decent. Growing wary after supper, I refuse the arrangement and choose the bar-room bench instead. The bench proves impossible and, after the landlord explains the head‑peddling business, I take the big upstairs bed alone. As I doze, the harpooneer returns, and I lie still watching him unpack a preserved head, bare his tattooed body, and worship his little idol at the fireplace. When he leaps into the dark bed with a lighted tomahawk-pipe and threatens, I shout for the landlord. The landlord makes peace, and I have Queequeg put away his pipe and tomahawk, accept him as my bedfellow, and sleep soundly.

caption_spine: I sought the landlord for a bed, and with the house full I agreed to share a harpooneer’s blanket—so long as he was not “decidedly objectionable.”
Growing suspicious of this dark-complexioned harpooneer, I told the landlord I’d changed my mind and would try the bar-room bench.
The bench proved a freezing folly, and when the landlord explained the head‑peddling, I let him lead me to the great cold bed and turned in alone.
Dozing, I saw the harpooneer enter with a light and a New Zealand head, strip to his tattooed squares, set up his little ebony idol in the fireplace, and pray over a biscuit blaze while I lay still.
Then out went the light, and the wild cannibal sprang into bed with a lighted tomahawk in his teeth, so I sang out for the landlord.
Peter Coffin brought a candle and peace, and I made Queequeg stash his pipe and tomahawk—better sleep with a sober cannibal than a drunken Christian—and I slept as sound as ever.
